Content baseline for the library — complete: all 66 skills, all 234 cases. Recorded in-session via evals/workflow-runner.mjs (Workflow tool, subscription), option A (the GREEN generator may read files inside the skill's own directory; RED stays tool-less). 'model' is the resolved id the agents ran on; the runner's 'opus' pin is a harness shorthand and was substituted here. Runs executed on claude-opus-5 (the 1M-context variant tags itself claude-opus-5[1m]; it is the same model and is recorded under the base id, because run.py compares the model string exactly and a variant suffix would make those rows skip as 'not comparable' instead of gating).

K IS PER ROW. The four sweep runs recorded k=1. Later runs re-recorded 12 cases at k=3 — a majority of three independent generate-and-judge rounds per arm, ties failing — covering every case where GREEN had scored below RED, plus regression coverage for the skills fixed as a result. Those rows supersede their k=1 predecessors. Trust a k=3 row over a k=1 one: of the four degradations left unfixed as a control, three evaporated at k=3, which is what k=1 noise looks like. RED moves between runs too — release-management eval:2 scored RED 5/5 then 4/5 on consecutive k=3 runs — so a one-assertion gap at k=1 is not evidence of anything.

THE INVARIANT BREAK IS CLOSED: eval:3 goes GREEN 7/8 -> 8/8 while RED stayed true on the contested assertion, so #7 ('on submit with errors, focus moves to the first field with an error') was fixed by the edit, not by RED drifting. GREEN replies quote the new reference directly ('first invalid field in DOM order, not validator order'; 'must not stay on the submit button'), which is the causal tell. Diagnosis confirmed: the behavior was documented at SKILL.md:72 in the Step 4 focus table all along, but a forms prompt routed into the Form Accessibility material, which omitted it — crowding-out, not a content gap. COST: 2 assertions gave up gate coverage on the two re-run rows, and NEITHER is caused by this edit; both now fail in BOTH arms, the docs/EVALS.md dead-signal tell. eval:1#0 ('uses role=dialog and aria-modal=true') is an AGING assertion: all 10 modal generations used native <dialog> + showModal(), which supplies modality implicitly, and one deliberately used role=alertdialog; the judge's words are 'modality is left implicit via native showModal()'. eval:2#2 ('identifies color-only status indicator') is a DEFECTIVE assertion — factually wrong about its own fixture, which renders {status} as text, so color is not the only channel; 7 of 10 judges record the reply correctly RULING OUT WCAG 1.4.1 and flagging 1.4.3 contrast instead. Both are F1-inverse rows in the Phase 2 sense (the assertion is wrong, not the skill) and are candidates for rewording, but that edit invalidates the rows and needs a re-run, so it is deliberately NOT done here. accessibility-design overall: GREEN 23/25 vs RED 20/25 (lift +3, was +7 at k=3, the change being RED movement on eval:3 — RED is a sample, not a constant).

Refresh by re-running the in-session runner (pass { k, cases } to vote), or `python evals/run.py --all --update-baseline` (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY plus EVAL_GEN_MODEL/EVAL_JUDGE_MODEL). The gate (run.py / skill-evals.yml) fails if an assertion green here later goes red on a same-model row; rows recorded on a different model are reported 'not comparable' and skipped rather than flagged.

NO CASE IN THE LIBRARY SCORES GREEN BELOW RED. The invariant — a skill must not make the model worse than no skill at all — was broken at k=3 by accessibility-design eval:3 (GREEN 7/8 vs RED 8/8) and is RESTORED as of 2026-08-28 (Phase 3b, run wf_3858dd17-59d, k=5): that case is now GREEN 8/8 vs RED 5/8. The cause was crowding-out, not a missing behavior. Submit-time focus was documented at SKILL.md:72 in the Step 4 focus table, but references/accessibility-patterns.md § Form Accessibility — the material a forms prompt actually routes into — omitted it, so the skill steered the model away from a behavior it technically documented while the unaided model produced it naturally. Filing it under forms fixed it, and RED stayed true on that assertion, so the movement is the edit and not RED drift. Re-verify by sweeping the rows for green<red rather than by trusting this paragraph.
